pages.text: Spinning is not free. Every machine uses some of the $(thing)stress capacity$() of its network, measured in $(bold)su$() (stress units). Sources provide capacity, machines consume it.
If the machines on a network ask for more than the sources give, it is $(bold)overstressed$(): the whole network stops, not just one machine. The fix is more sources, fewer machines, or slower speed.

pages.title: Stressometer
pages.text: A gauge that shows how much of a network's capacity is in use. With goggles on, it names the exact numbers.
$(bold)Faster costs more.$() A machine's stress cost goes up with its RPM, and a source's capacity goes up with RPM as well. A fast network can carry more, but each machine on it also eats more.

$(bold)Reading it.$() Wear $(l:create_basics/tools_wrench)Goggles$(/l) and look at a machine for its Stress Impact, or a source for its Stress Capacity. Item tooltips (hold Shift) say Low, Moderate or High stress impact.

pages.title: Engineer's Goggles
pages.text: Shows Kinetic Stats on any machine: impact, capacity and speed. Steam boilers show their power level too.

Large sources such as $(l:create_basics/power_sources)large water wheels and steam engines$(/l) exist because a lot of machines need a lot of capacity. Exact numbers vary by config, so check the goggles in your own world.
